title: Arathi Highlands
body: The Arathi Highlands are a country of rolling green hills and scattered pines, and the birthplace of the first human nation. Here Thoradin united the human tribes into the Empire of Arathor and raised Strom, its first capital, with a great wall to hold back the Amani trolls. The Trollbane kings who later ruled Stromgarde from the old capital warred with the Witherbark trolls for generations. Those days are gone. King Thoras Trollbane is dead and his city lies in ruins, carved up between Prince Galen's militia, the outlaws of the Syndicate and the Boulderfist ogres. The last soldiers of Stromgarde hold Refuge Pointe in the heart of the highlands, while in the northeast the Horde has rebuilt Hammerfall on the site of an old orc internment camp. Witherbark warbands and ogres press them all. Beneath the hills, a voice calls out through glowing crystals, begging to be set free, and on the southern coast a pirate crew sits marooned in Faldir's Cove.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Arathi_Highlands (Thoradin, Arathor, Strom, Thoradin's Wall, Trollbane feud with Witherbark, Stromgarde overrun, Refuge Pointe, Hammerfall internment camp)
quest 638 description (Thoras dead, Stromgarde in ruins)
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide and nothing from a later era. Thoras's death and the ruin of Stromgarde are the state of the land on arrival; the voice beneath the hills is told only as a plea. Arathi Basin (League of Arathor, Defilers) stays out: it is a battleground, and mod-individual-progression only sets its level brackets from state 0. Earlier: Opening line softened from 'oldest human land in the Eastern Kingdoms' (unsourced) to the birthplace of Arathor; rest verified against the wiki and quests 638, 681.

title: Thoradin's Wall
body: From the highlands, Thoradin's Wall marks the western edge of the land, a long line of weathered stone between Arathi and the foothills beyond. The ruins of Stromgarde, the city it was raised to guard, still lie near it, but the wall has held no army back for a very long time. Highland striders hunt along its foot and plains creepers crawl among its fallen stones. The highlands it once sheltered now face ogres, outlaws and the Witherbark all at once, and the old barrier stops none of them.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Thoradin's_Wall (built by Thoradin near Strom against Amani incursions; separates Arathi from Hillsbrad; heavily damaged and in ruins in original WoW)
posarea.py: area 1857 found on the western edge between Hillsbrad and Arathi
zone_areas: Highland Strider 2559 and Plains Creeper 2563 spawn in area 1857
notes: Deduplicated 2026-10-19: the wall's building by King Thoradin and his capital of Strom are told only in hillsbrad.json 26713 (which owns the wall's history); this entry keeps the Arathi side and names Stromgarde only as the ruins near it. Dropped the unsourced 'oldest works of human hands' and 'greatest threat' lines. Galen's Fall (Cataclysm) left out.

title: Northfold Manor
body: Northfold Manor is a farm estate on the northwestern edge of the highlands. After Stromgarde fell, the Syndicate seized it as an outpost, and highwaymen, mercenaries and pathstalkers now hold its fields and barns. From here the outlaws command the country between Refuge Pointe and Southshore, so that the supplies the Stromgarde defenders need from Hillsbrad rarely get through. Worse things have happened here than banditry. The shaman Tor'gan of Hammerfall traced a burning unease in his blood to the manor and found the traces of demonic summoning, with a spent bloodstone amulet lying on the ground. A rarely seen outlaw called Singer lurks in the small house.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Northfold_Manor (farm, Syndicate outpost after Stromgarde fell, Singer in the small house)

title: Boulder'gor
body: Boulder'gor is an ogre mound in the western highlands, northeast of the ruins of Stromgarde. Boulderfist ogres and enforcers crowd its camps, and Witherbark trolls come and go among them, a sign of the pact the two peoples have made against their common enemies. A brutish ogre named Kovork is sometimes found there. For the Horde, the mound serves as a proving ground: Tallow of Tarren Mill sends would-be recruits here to test their strength before they are trusted to join the defenders of Hammerfall.

title: The Circles of Binding
body: Four rings of standing stones lie scattered across the highlands: the Circles of West, East and Outer Binding, and the strongest of them, the Circle of Inner Binding, close to the ruins of Stromgarde. Each holds a Stone of Binding, and together they pin something deep beneath the earth. Elemental exiles keep watch over them: creatures of flame at the western circle, of water in the east, of thunder at the outer ring and of rumbling stone at the inner one, where a Keystone stands among the stones as a final lock. Near the eastern circle walks Fozruk, a stone watcher who carries the key to that lock, attended by a small band of kobolds.
sources: quest 651 description and objectives (four Stones of Binding, Inner the strongest, keys from West, East, Outer)

title: Stromgarde Keep
body: Once Strom, the first capital of humankind, Stromgarde was long the seat of the Trollbane kings. Now it is a ruin and a battlefield. Prince Galen Trollbane's militia holds the quarter around the chapel and the Sanctum behind it, where King Thoras lies entombed with the sword Trol'kalar. The Syndicate under Lord Falconcrest commands the inner keep, while the Boulderfist ogres, Witherbark berserkers at their side, have taken the old mage district and the Tower of Arathor, whose master, Archmage Trelane, tried to hold it and failed. None of the three can drive out the others, and the bloody stalemate grinds on while the defenders dwindle.

title: Faldir's Cove
body: On the rugged southern coast lies Faldir's Cove, named, it seems, for Faldir, the descendant of Thoradin who led his followers away from Arathor to found the kingdom of Stormwind. Today it shelters the Harbinger, the one ship of Captain Shakes O'Breen's Blackwater Raiders to come in safely. The pirates sailed from Booty Bay after a lost elven treasure, but as the other two ships followed the Harbinger in, the sea rumbled, the tide fell away and both were wrecked on the reef. The survivors now camp beside the water with a pair of gnomish inventors, unable to leave until the tide rises and the naga stop watching.

title: The Drowned Reef
body: Off the coast southwest of Faldir's Cove lies the Drowned Reef, and it is not only a reef. Sunken stonework, something like a temple, lies beneath the waves, guarded by the Daggerspine naga, and it is said the strange tide that wrecked the Blackwater Raiders was their doing. The Maiden's Folly and the Spirit of Silverpine ran aground on it and sank so fast that few escaped, and the naga slew the survivors in the water. The ships' logs and charts still lie in the wrecks, and somewhere in these waters, if a gnomish contraption is to be believed, lies the lost elven treasure that brought the Raiders here. A naga called Prince Nazjak hunts the reef.
sources: quest 662 description (ships ran aground on some sort of temple in the reef, sank quickly; logs and charts)
quest 664 description (naga killed all the survivors)
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Faldir's_Cove (tide caused by the naga guarding sunken ruins)

Earlier: verified. 'Few escaped' softened from quest 664, where Steelgut alone seems to have survived from his crew. Checked: the naga-caused tide stays as hearsay; it is the wiki's pre-Cataclysm (World of Warcraft) history of Faldir's Cove, and quests 662, 663 and 669 (tide fell as the ships neared a temple in the reef, creatures disturbed) fit it.

parts.body: The reef did hold the treasure. Elven gems lie scattered across the sea floor, so long under the water that they have calcified into thick stone and can hardly be told from the rocks around them. Only through gnomish goggles, charged in the cursed cave above the cove, can they be picked out of the dark sea, beneath the eyes of the naga.
sources: quest 666 description and reward text (gems calcified, goggles)

title: Refuge Pointe
body: Refuge Pointe, in the heart of the highlands, is the last stronghold of the kingdom of Stromgarde. When the city fell, the remnants of its army refused to abandon the land and withdrew here, and under Captain Nials they have sworn not to leave until the king's banner flies over Stromgarde once more. It is a spare camp of tents, a forge, a few merchants and a gryphon roost, ringed by defenders, and its wanted board posts the militia's bounties on Syndicate leaders. Two agents of Archmage Malin of Stormwind, the dwarf Skuerto and Apprentice Kryten, have also made camp here, sent to recover what Archmage Trelane left behind when the city fell.

title: Dabyrie's Farmstead
body: In the north of the highlands stands Dabyrie's Farmstead, home of a family that still holds to the kingdom of Stromgarde. Kenata Dabyrie keeps the farm with her children Fardel and Marcel, and a crew of laborers works the fields under the protection of the Dabyrie Militia. Not everyone is glad that they prospered. In the Undercity, the Forsaken Genavie Callow, who lost her family to the plague and saw her estate looted and burned in the war, swears the Dabyries stole the last precious things she owned, and she wants all of their heads for it.

title: Go'Shek Farm
body: Go'Shek Farm, in the east of the highlands, has been taken over by the Horde to help feed Hammerfall, and peons work its fields under the watch of grunts. Not all of its business is farming. Forsaken bodyguards stand over a small house to the south, home to Apothecary Jorell, who promises anyone who troubles him that he will find a use for their body once he has killed them, and swears that no one will stop the Forsaken. Such company draws notice: a pair of watchers sent from Southshore keep a quiet eye on the farm from hiding, suspecting the Forsaken of some dark work.

title: Hammerfall
body: Hammerfall stands in the northeast of the highlands on ground the orcs remember with bitterness. After the Second War this was one of the largest of the human internment camps, where captured orcs were held behind wood and steel. Thrall and Orgrim Doomhammer stormed it to free the prisoners, and in that battle a knight charged Doomhammer from behind and ran him through with his lance, a mortal wound. When the Horde returned to the highlands, it raised an outpost on the ruins and named it in the fallen warchief's honor. Now Drum Fel leads its defense against the Boulderfist ogres and Witherbark trolls, who have joined forces to drive the Horde out.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Hammerfall (one of the largest internment camps, freed by Thrall and Doomhammer, Doomhammer mortally wounded by a knight's lance, named in his honor, Drum Fel)

title: Drywhisker Gorge
body: Drywhisker Gorge cuts into the hills east of Hammerfall and ends in a cave held by the Drywhisker kobolds. The voice that speaks through the Shards of Myzrael names them allies of the giants who hold her captive beneath Arathi, and they carry motes of her power. Nearby, a cluster of iridescent shards juts from the rock, much like the Shards of Myzrael, though it lacks their reassuring warmth. The gorge is also the only known source of lesser bloodstone ore, and the kobold geomancer Flintdagger is sometimes seen among the diggers and surveyors.

title: Witherbark Village
body: In the southeast of the highlands, around a small lake, lies Witherbark Village, home of the forest trolls who have been sworn enemies of Stromgarde for generations. Axe throwers, headhunters and witch doctors fill the huts, while the shadow hunters, the strongest of whom carry a special knife earned in their rites of passage, keep to a large cavern behind the village where the tribe's leaders are often found, among them the warband leader Zalas Witherbark. A second warband leader, Nimar the Slayer, also stalks the village. The Witherbark have made common cause with the Boulderfist ogres, and together they have set out to drive the Horde from Hammerfall.

title: Boulderfist Hall
body: Boulderfist Hall is an ogre stronghold in the south of the highlands, east of the Thandol Span. Brutes and magi of the Boulderfist clan hold it, and the defenders of Hammerfall count them a harder foe than the Witherbark. A hulking ogre known as Molok the Crusher is sometimes found there, and among the hall's ogres is one named Kor'gresh Coldrage, who bellows that he will smash his foes and fights with blasts of freezing cold.
sources: quest 693 description (south of Refuge Pointe, east of Thandol Span; Kor'gresh's ice blasts)
quest 678 description (maulers and magi a greater challenge)

parts.body: The ice is not his own. A dwarf scouting for Archmage Malin of Stormwind learned that Kor'gresh carries the Wand of Invocation, left behind by Archmage Trelane when Stromgarde fell, and from the blasts of ice the ogre throws at his own kin to keep them in line, judged him close to mastering all of its powers.

title: Thandol Span
body: The Thandol Span comes to ground at the southern tip of the highlands, and the Arathi end of the crossing is no safer than the Wetlands side. Dark Iron shadowcasters, bombardiers and suppliers have made camp on the slopes just beyond the bridge. Out on the span, the dwarf sentry Foggy MacKreel nurses a sore head. He drank too much moonshine and slept through his watch, and recalls only a rumbling overhead, as if a whole brigade of siege engines had rolled past. He fears Longbraid would have his head if he knew, and frets about a moonshine debt he owes a brewmeister in Southshore.

title: Captain Nials
body: Captain Nials commands the remnants of the Stromgarde army at Refuge Pointe. Her city has fallen, and honor and duty bind her soldiers to the highlands until the king's banner flies over Stromgarde once more. She knows the war is going badly. Her ranks thin while the enemy grows, the help she needs from Southshore must pass through land the Syndicate holds, and inside the city the Syndicate pays its rabble a bounty in gold on the badge of every militiaman they kill. Nials will not let the cutthroats keep trophies of her brave dead, and she wants every one of those badges brought back.
sources: creature_text 2700 (reading the names, So many lost)
notes: Converted: the badges' return and her reading of the names moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 682, which needs 681, so Northfold's cleared road is told there too). Dropped her refusal of the Wetlands dwarves: it is the turn-in of Wetlands quest 634, told in wetlands 1120 and 1129 part 4. Gossip 11881 (npc_text 16661, broadcast 44809, Cataclysm-era) is not used. Faction 1: Nials uses faction template 12 (Stormwind), hostile to Horde. Checked: part 1's last line reworded off the 682 reward text and away from 4526 part 2. Gossip 11881 (npc_text 16661) still unused.

parts.body: With Northfold Manor's outlaws cut down, more supplies get through from Southshore, and Nials dares to hope her cause is not lost. When the badges come back, she searches through them and reads the names aloud, private after private, then sighs that so many have been lost, and so many more must be before the battle ends. Word will go to every family that its soldier died fighting: hard tidings to carry, yet kinder than leaving them to wonder.

title: Prince Galen Trollbane
body: Galen Trollbane is the son of King Thoras Trollbane and heir to a kingdom in ruins. With his father dead, he leads the militia that holds part of Stromgarde, keeping to a chapel deep in the city beside the Sanctum where Thoras lies entombed with the ancestral sword Trol'kalar. To guard the tomb, the sigils that unseal it were divided among the survivors: the sigil of Thoradin Galen broke into pieces and gave to his defenders, the sigil of Arathor went to his cavalry leader Valorcall, and the sigil of Trollbane he keeps on his own person. He is well guarded and a capable warrior in his own right.

quest 639 description (sigils divided among the survivors)

parts.body: Prince Galen's guards could not save him. He was cut down in his chapel deep in the militia-held quarter of Stromgarde, beside the Sanctum where his father lies entombed, and the defenders of the ruined city lost the prince who led them.

title: Lord Falconcrest and Otto
body: The Syndicate is a brotherhood of outlaws led by nobles of fallen Alterac, and in the Arathi Highlands its efforts are directed by Lord Falconcrest from the ruins of Stromgarde. His outlaws hold the inner keep, and the Syndicate's leaders pay their rabble gold for every badge taken from a dead Stromgarde soldier. At Falconcrest's side stands his bodyguard Otto, no strategist but a fierce fighter who has killed dozens of the city's defenders, and who assures his master that everything is going as planned. The Stromgarde militia has put a price on both their heads.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Syndicate (led by nobles of fallen Alterac; Falconcrest commands in Stromgarde)
DB spawns: Falconcrest 2597 and Otto 2599 at 26,65.7 in area 324
notes: Converted: their deaths are parts 1 (Otto: KILL 2599 or QUEST_DONE 685) and 2 (Falconcrest: KILL 2597 or QUEST_DONE 685), split because either can fall first; both factions can kill them. The Syndicate's Alterac nobles stay general, as in Hillsbrad's and Alterac's openings; no Perenolde, Vardus or Argus Wake. Earlier: verified. Faction 0: both are faction template 16, hostile to everyone, so both factions can kill them. The Argus Wake connection is left out (not shown in 3.3.5 Arathi content). 'No strategist' paraphrases quest 685 (not a strategic target). Checked: Otto's line is out-of-combat chatter (smart_scripts 2599), so part 1 no longer makes it his dying words. Both parts confirmed: either can die first, and QUEST_DONE 685 shows both.

parts.body: Otto's assurances came to nothing. The bodyguard who had cut down dozens of Stromgarde's defenders was slain at last in the inner keep, and his promise to Lord Falconcrest that victory was only a matter of time died with him.

Lord Falconcrest was struck down in the inner keep from which he had directed the Syndicate's war on Stromgarde. The militia had hoped that his death would throw the outlaws' efforts in the highlands into disarray, though his rabble holds the keep still.

title: Marez Cowl
body: Marez Cowl is a warlock and a high-ranking advisor and operative of the Syndicate, last seen in the outlaw-held quarter of Stromgarde. She is skilled and cunning, and she traffics openly with demons, calling them forth in great numbers from within the city walls. Those who hunt her are warned to take the greatest care. Refuge Pointe and Hammerfall agree on little, but each has its own reasons to want her dead.
sources: quest 684 description and reward text (high-level advisor and operative, warlock trafficking with demons, emissary to a darker power)
quest 673 description and reward text (warlock in Stromgarde summoning demons with a bloodstone orb)
quest 671 completion text (burning in the blood)
DB spawns: Marez Cowl 2783 at 29.6,63 in area 324
notes: Converted: Nials's rumor of the darker power moved to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 684; Alliance-only part), her death to part 1 (KILL 2783, QUEST_DONE 684 or 673). Tor'gan's burning blood and the bloodstone orb left the opening: tracing the summoning to her is Tor'gan's reveal (4522 part 2, QUEST_ACCEPT 673), and the orb's fate is his part 3. The rumor is Arathi's own text and names no one, so it does not give away Alterac's Argus Wake. Pronoun follows quest 684 (she). Faction 0: faction template 16, killable by both, and each faction has a quest for her. Checked: part 2 reworded (was near the 684 reward text and 4526 part 3). The rumor names no one and does not give away Alterac's Argus Wake (3617 part 1).

parts.body: Her demons could not save her. Marez Cowl was hunted down in the Syndicate's quarter of Stromgarde and slain among the outlaws she served, and the Syndicate in the highlands lost one of its most cunning advisors.

At Refuge Pointe, Captain Nials paid the bounty gladly. Marez had long been a danger to the city's defenders, and a whisper ran among them that troubled the captain more: the warlock may have been a go-between for the Syndicate and some other, darker power. If the whisper was true, that power has lost its envoy in the highlands.

title: Drum Fel and Korin Fel
body: Drum Fel leads the defense of Hammerfall, a hard warrior with little patience for the untested and no time even to sharpen his axe. He sends every able fighter against the Witherbark and Boulderfist warbands that besiege the outpost, praising courage and scorning cowardice in equal measure, and believes Hammerfall will thrive in the highlands once its enemies are broken. His wife, Korin Fel, a seer, lives beside him at the outpost and loves him dearly.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Hammerfall (Drum Fel led the settlement, believed it would thrive)
notes: Converted: Korin's secret moved to part 1 (QUEST_ACCEPT 680, whose description holds it; 680 has no prerequisite, so it is offered on talking to her, but the TALK opening no longer tells it), Or'Kalar's death to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 680). Drum's belief that Hammerfall will thrive stays as his belief (quest 679 reward text, the wiki). Faction 2: both use faction template 125, hostile to Alliance. Earlier: Dropped npc_text 17772 (Cataclysm-era broadcast text). Checked: opening drops 'would do anything to keep him safe', which hinted at her secret; 'seer' stays (talking to her shows 680). Parts 1 and 2 reworded away from 4528 parts 3 and 4.

parts.body: Korin's auguries have shown her what her husband cannot see. The ogre Or'Kalar, beaten by Drum years ago and hating him ever since, is behind the attacks and has set a trap for him. Sure that Drum would charge off to meet his old enemy, she keeps every trace of the ogre from him and quietly asks others to kill Or'Kalar in his place. Some may call her silence weak or dishonorable; to her it is a different kind of strength.

In time Or'Kalar's head was laid before her. Drum would never walk into the ogre's trap, and Korin, with her husband and the outpost safe for another day, rewarded the courage of those who had spared him.

title: Gor'mul
body: Gor'mul is an orc warrior of the old Horde who was once a prisoner in the internment camp that stood where Hammerfall is now. He saw Orgrim Doomhammer come in his midnight plate to free the camp, and saw a knight on horseback run the Warchief through from behind. As the earth shook and the other prisoners escaped, Gor'mul was left behind, and he wandered alone and without hope for years until the Horde returned. He has never recovered from Doomhammer's death, and the shaman Tor'gan hopes that the shamanic power the Horde has found again may wake the warrior in him.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Gor'mul (orc warrior of the Old Horde)
notes: Converted: his scorn for the amulet moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 674, where 675 is offered), his awakening to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 702 at Gor'mul, creature_text 2792, or QUEST_DONE 847). Faction 2: Gor'mul uses faction template 29 (Orgrimmar) and quest 655 is Horde-only. His later role as a quest giver (Cataclysm) is left out. Checked: part 1's 'Tor'gan's pity' came from 702's request text; now kept to 675.

parts.body: Trinkets do not move him. Handed an amulet of raptor bone, Gor'mul asked what use he had for polished bone and flung it to the ground. Mercy, he said, was denied him on the day he was not allowed to die beside his Warchief, and he cannot see why Tor'gan should show him any.

Tor'gan's orb did what the amulet could not. As its power stirred his blood, Gor'mul felt the guile of the raptor slip through him and cried that his strength was returning. The power of the shamans had convinced him, for the time being, and he agreed to listen to what Tor'gan had to say.

title: Tor'gan
body: Tor'gan is a troll shaman of Hammerfall, a practitioner of the shamanic magic the Horde has found anew under its young Warchief Thrall. He has spent much patience on Gor'mul, crafting amulets and orbs filled with the spirit of the raptor in the hope of waking the warrior within. He feels fouler magic too. A strangeness in the air simmers in his blood, and the search for its source led him west to Northfold Manor, where he found the traces of demonic summoning and a drained bloodstone amulet left behind.
sources: quest 640 description (Tor'gan, the troll shaman) and reward text
notes: Converted: the rebound sigil moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 640), the warlock in Stromgarde to part 2 (QUEST_ACCEPT 673, offered after 671; who is behind the summoning is the reveal), the orb to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 673). Faction 2: faction template 126 (Darkspear). He has no gossip menu but starts and ends quests, so the quest dialog serves for TALK. Checked: 'five pieces' dropped (mod-individual-progression sets 11 fragments for 640).

parts.body: When the scattered pieces of the sigil of Thoradin, which Prince Galen had divided among Stromgarde's defenders, were laid before him, Tor'gan judged its magical structure easy to reform. He bound the pieces whole again in a flash of power, and found it easier than he had expected.

The amulets from Northfold told him that the Syndicate dabbles in dark, demonic magic, and Tor'gan traced its source to Stromgarde. A powerful warlock dwells within its walls and, with an arcane relic, summons terrible demons in large numbers. The burning in his blood grows by the day, and he has vowed to destroy that relic so that it can taint the land no longer.

Marez Cowl's bloodstone orb came into his hands at last, and Tor'gan promised that his restless nights would turn to peaceful slumber once it was destroyed. It reminded him, chillingly, of the power the demons once held over the orcs, before Hellscream released them from their curse.

title: Or'Kalar
body: Or'Kalar is a Boulderfist ogre who leads his clan's forces in the ruins of Stromgarde, a pawn of Mug'thol. He lurks near the Tower of Arathor, in the old mage district the Boulderfist have overrun, among the ogres and Witherbark berserkers who hold that quarter of the city against the militia and the Syndicate alike. Ogres crowd all around the tower, and few reach it without a fight.
sources: quest 680 description, completion and reward texts (Mug'thol's pawn, hatred of Drum Fel, trap, near the Tower of Arathor, his death stops the attacks)
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Boulderfist_clan (Or'Kalar led the Boulderfist forces in Stromgarde, answers to Mug'thol)
DB spawns: Or'Kalar 2773, 7 spawn points at 18-21,65-69 in area 324
quest 694 description (ogres all around the Tower of Arathor)
DB spawns within 80 yards of Trelane's Chest 2716: Boulderfist Shaman 2570 x6, Boulderfist Lord 2571 x6, Boulderfist Mauler 2569, Or'Kalar 2773 x5 (visible to both factions)
notes: Converted: his grudge against Drum Fel and the trap moved to part 1 (QUEST_ACCEPT 680; Horde-only part), his death to part 2 (KILL 2773 or QUEST_DONE 680), kept to what a kill alone shows. The opening keeps his rank and haunt (wiki, spawns). Faction 0: Or'Kalar is faction template 45, hostile to both. Checked: the ogres around the tower are visible spawns for both factions (added source), so the opening reads true for the Horde too.

parts.body: Or'Kalar's quarrel is personal. Years ago he was beaten by Drum Fel of Hammerfall, and he has hated him ever since. The attacks on Hammerfall are his doing, a trap laid to draw Drum out to his death, and only Drum's wife Korin, who saw it in her auguries, knows it.
Or'Kalar was slain at last among the ruins near the Tower of Arathor, struck down amid the ogres he led, and the Boulderfist in Stromgarde lost the chieftain Mug'thol had set over them.

title: Myzrael
body: Myzrael calls herself a princess of the earth, held captive deep beneath the Arathi Highlands by the giants. Her only voice in the world above comes through crystal shards that break the surface in the northern hills, and through them she pleads for rescue, stirring a feeling of warmth and safety in all who listen. She names the giants her captors and the Drywhisker kobolds their allies, and asks only for help in breaking the wards that pin her beneath the earth, promising that her gratitude will shake its very foundations.
sources: quest 635 description (vision of the northern mountains)
quest 656 description and reward text (warmth and security)
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Myzrael (earth elemental princess imprisoned by giants)
notes: Converted: her release moved to part 1 (QUEST_ACCEPT 653 Alliance or 688 Horde, offered at the Keystone right after 652; their text is her cry of freedom), the Twilight's Hammer to part 2 (QUEST_ACCEPT 687, from Gerrig Bonegrip or Zaruk; the two are left unnamed since each side meets only its own), her betrayal and defeat to part 3 (KILL 2755, summoned only during 656, or QUEST_DONE 656). Theldurin's own warning stays Badlands' (320, 330 on 692). Old Gods madness and Deepholm (Cataclysm) left out. Earlier: Myzrael is summoned (event_scripts 420, summon creature 2755) at the Shards during quest 656, so the KILL trigger works for both factions. Checked: part 3 (KILL 2755 or QUEST_DONE 656) trimmed to her outburst and defeat, which a kill shows; the binding with her shackles is new part 4 on QUEST_DONE 656. Part 2 reworded away from 4530 part 3. Badlands 320 and 330 do not tell her defeat and use neither 656 nor 2755.

parts.body: With the Keystone broken, Myzrael cried out that she was free: free to gather strength hidden from the giants, who would overpower and imprison her again if they faced her now, but who in time would regret their wardship of her. She called her rescuer a noble ally, and promised to call on them again to summon her to the surface when she was ready.

Her allies were waiting. The friend she named greeted her rescuer as one who served the same higher cause, and the truth came out: they were cultists of the Twilight's Hammer, who call Myzrael their Lady and mean to see her return. The scroll that could summon her had been carried off by a renegade of their order, Theldurin the Lost, said to hide in the Badlands.

Called up at the Shards of Myzrael before her time, the princess demanded to know why she had been summoned before reaching her full power, then named her rescuer a fool for helping her and attacked. She was beaten all the same.
sources: event_scripts 420 (Myzrael summoned at the Shards during quest 656)

parts.body: Then she was bound once more. Her own Eldritch Shackles, fastened about the Shards, hold her beneath the earth again, and the crystals that once soothed every listener now carry only her ill will toward the world above.
sources: quest 656 description (she will again be trapped) and reward text

title: Shakes O'Breen
body: Captain Shakes O'Breen of the Blackwater Raiders led three ships out of Booty Bay to Faldir's Cove, steered by one of Professor Phizzlethorpe's contraptions toward a lost elven treasure. Only his own ship, the Harbinger, came through: the sea gave a rumble, the water dropped away beneath the other two, and both crashed into the reef, which he is sure is no mere reef. He fears Fleet Master Seahorn will have his ship once he hears of the loss. Until the tide rises he is stranded in the cove with his crew, a pair of gnomes and the survivors of the wrecks, promising a handsome reward to anyone who helps them.
notes: Converted: Seahorn's verdict moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 669, turned in to Seahorn in Booty Bay; an Arathi quest used by no other file), the naga attack and his reasons to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 667, the last of the chain). Faction 0: O'Breen uses faction template 121 (friendly to both) and his quests have AllowableRaces 0. Earlier: Booty Bay as the home port comes from quests 663 and 669. Checked: QUEST_DONE 669 unused elsewhere; stranglethorn 3323 does not mention O'Breen.

parts.body: Seahorn took the news better than O'Breen feared. Shown a sample of the elven gems as proof that the treasure had been found, the fleet master declared that he had always known good old Shakes was the right captain for the mission, and sent secret word back to him.

Then the Daggerspine gathered to strike. The naga would keep coming until he was dead, and though O'Breen does not value his own life above his crew's, they could never reach Booty Bay without his knowledge of the seas. He held the high ground beside the cannon as the naga came out of the sea, and his crew lived to wait out the low tide.

title: The Defenders of Stromgarde
body: From Refuge Pointe, Captain Nials fights a war she is losing. Her soldiers, the Syndicate and the ogres have divided Stromgarde in a bloody stalemate, and while her ranks thin, the enemy's swell. Help must come from Southshore, but the Syndicate holds the land between, so the outlaws of Northfold Manor must be cleared before the supply trains can get through. Inside the city, Syndicate leaders pay their rabble gold for every badge cut from a fallen militiaman, and Nials will not let them profit from her dead. The wanted board at Refuge Pointe names the true targets: Marez Cowl, a cunning warlock who traffics with demons, and Lord Falconcrest and his bodyguard Otto, whose deaths would throw the Syndicate's efforts in the highlands into disarray.
notes: Converted: the opening is the setup of 681, 682, 684 and 685; the rumor about Marez (684 reward text) left it. Parts: 1 Northfold cleared (QUEST_DONE 681), 2 the badges (QUEST_DONE 682), 3 Marez (QUEST_DONE 684), 4 Falconcrest and Otto (QUEST_DONE 685). Faction 1: 681 has AllowableRaces 0 but its only giver, Captain Nials, is Stormwind-faction; 682, 684, 685 are Alliance-only. Checked: parts 2, 3 and 4 reworded away from the 682, 684 and 685 reward texts and from 4516 part 1 and 4519 part 2.

parts.body: The outlaws of Northfold Manor were cut down, and with them the pressure on the road from Southshore eased. More supplies began to reach Refuge Pointe, and for the first time in a long while Nials allowed that her cause might yet have hope.

The badges came home. One by one Nials read out the names of the fallen and sighed at the cost, already counting the losses still to come before the city could be won. Each family would at least learn that its soldier had died in battle.

Marez Cowl's head was laid before Nials, and the captain was glad of it. The warlock had threatened her soldiers in the city, and some said she had carried the Syndicate's dealings with a darker power still.

The heads of Lord Falconcrest and Otto were brought to Refuge Pointe, and Nials counted the bounty money well spent. The man who directed the Syndicate's efforts in the highlands and the bodyguard who had killed dozens of her defenders were both dead.

title: Trelane's Treasures
body: When Stromgarde fell, Archmage Trelane tried and failed to hold the Tower of Arathor, then fled to Stormwind, leaving his belongings behind. His former apprentice, Archmage Malin, has sent two agents to recover them, the gruff dwarf Skuerto and Apprentice Kryten, who have made camp at Refuge Pointe and asked Malin for more help. Skuerto is off scouting and has no time for newcomers. Kryten, kinder, sets them to gathering the reagents Malin wants from the Witherbark trolls of the southeast: tusks, medicine pouches and the special knife the strongest shadow hunters carry after their rites of passage.
sources: quest 691 description, completion and reward text
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Stromgarde_Keep (Trelane failed to defend the Tower and exiled himself to Stormwind)
notes: Converted: the opening is the setup of 690 and 691 (npc_text 3294: Skuerto busy scouting). Parts: 1 the wand found (QUEST_ACCEPT 693), 2 the wand recovered (QUEST_DONE 693), 3 the tower raided (QUEST_DONE 696), 4 Malin's delight (QUEST_DONE 697, turned in to Malin in Stormwind; an Arathi chain quest used by no other file). Faction 1: all quests are Alliance-only; Skuerto (2789, faction template 55 Ironforge) and Kryten (2788, faction template 1078 Stormwind) are hostile to Horde. Skuerto's gossip 16390 (Danath, Cataclysm) stays unused. Trelane's flight to Stormwind is from the wiki. Checked: QUEST_DONE 697 unused elsewhere; stormwind.json never names Malin or Trelane. Skuerto's 16390 unused.

parts.body: Skuerto came back from Boulderfist Hall looking as if he had tangled with the ogres, though he would rather no one mentioned it. He had found where the first of Trelane's treasures had gone: the ogre Kor'gresh Coldrage had the Wand of Invocation and, judging by the ice he hurled at his own kin, was close to mastering it.

The wand came back from Boulderfist Hall. Three items remained on Skuerto's list, all of them in Stromgarde, in the Tower of Arathor that the ogres now surround, and the dwarf set about planning the next phase.

The plan worked. An azure agate taken from the Boulderfist shaman, who had carried such gems off from the tower, was enchanted by Kryten into a key and pressed to a pedestal at the tower's foot, waking its old defenses. Under the ogres' noses, Trelane's phylactery, orb and ember agate were carried out of their chests, and Skuerto declared the mission an overwhelming success.
sources: DB: Runed Pedestal 2715 and Trelane's Chest 2716, Footlocker 2717, Lockbox 2718 at 18,67-69

parts.body: In Stormwind, Archmage Malin opened Skuerto's sealed letter and his eyes grew wide. By the Light, it was done. Trelane would be so pleased, and Kryten and Skuerto were on their way home with what had been lost.

title: Hammerfall Besieged
body: Hammerfall is under constant attack. In Tarren Mill, Tallow tests would-be defenders against the ogres of Boulder'gor before sending them on to Drum Fel, who names the enemy plainly: the Witherbark trolls, who turned their backs on the Horde, and the Boulderfist ogres, who would make meat and bedding of orcs, have joined forces to drive Hammerfall from the land. Drum means to show them that the Horde has a home here too. His champions begin with the Witherbark camps to the south, where they are to slay the trolls in droves and return only when the camps run thick with blood.
notes: Converted: the opening is the setup of 676 and 677. Parts: 1 the Witherbark and the ogre lair (QUEST_DONE 678), 2 the Boulderfist lords (QUEST_DONE 679), 3 Korin's secret (QUEST_ACCEPT 680, which has no prerequisite and is an entry trigger), 4 Or'Kalar slain (QUEST_DONE 680). Faction 2: all quests Horde-only. Tallow's race is not stated, so it is omitted. Checked: Tallow and 676 are not told in hillsbrad.json; 676 is used by no other file.

parts.body: The trolls bled first, then the ogres. In the Boulderfist lair toward the dwarven bridge, the maulers and magi who had long been the harder foe fell in turn. Drum named the last target: the head of the beast, the Boulderfist lords and their shaman who direct the attacks from the ruins of Stromgarde.

The Boulderfist lords and their shaman fell among the ruins of Stromgarde. Drum judged the threat greatly lessened, praised those who struck the blow for doing their people proud, and declared himself sure that Hammerfall would begin to thrive in the highlands.

Drum's wife Korin knows what he does not: why Hammerfall is under attack. The ogre Or'Kalar, Mug'thol's pawn in Stromgarde, has hated her husband since Drum defeated him years ago, and her auguries tell her he has laid a trap for him. She has hidden every sign of the ogre from Drum, who would rush off to face him, and quietly asks for Or'Kalar's head instead.

Or'Kalar died near the Tower of Arathor, and his head was brought to Korin. The trap he had laid would catch no one, and Drum's life and the safety of Hammerfall were protected, as Korin put it, for another day.

title: Trol'kalar
body: In the days of Arathor, Lord Ignaeus of Strom, called Trollbane, rode against the trolls with Trol'kalar, whose name means troll slayer, and for generations Strom and Arathor ravaged the trolls with it. With Thoras Trollbane dead and Stromgarde in ruins, Vol'jin resolved to take the sword for the Darkspear and turn it on the trolls of Zul'Gurub, and sent the hunter Zengu to Hammerfall to see it done. The blade lies in Thoras's tomb behind wards that only certain sigils can break, and those sigils were divided among the survivors of Stromgarde. The first, Zengu believes, was taken by the Syndicate and is carried by one of their agents in the city.
sources: quest 646 reward text (Strom and Arathor ravaged the trolls)
notes: Converted: the opening is the setup of 638 and 639. Parts: 1 the sigils of Strom and Thoradin (QUEST_DONE 641), 2 Valorcall, Galen and the Sigil of Ignaeus (QUEST_DONE 644), 3 the sword released and sent to Grom'gol (QUEST_DONE 646). Faction 2: every quest is Horde-only. Zengu's later death and the sword's return to Stromgarde (Cataclysm retcon) are left out. Checked: 'five pieces' dropped (mod-individual-progression sets 11 fragments for 640); part 1 reworded away from 4522 part 1.

parts.body: The sigil of Strom was taken from the Syndicate. The second, the sigil of Thoradin, Prince Galen had broken into pieces and shared among his defenders. Gathered and laid before Tor'gan, the pieces were made one again, and Zengu counted the work half done, though the holders of the third sigil roam the highlands.

The third, the sigil of Arathor, was won from Lieutenant Valorcall, leader of Galen's cavalry, a heavy blow to Stromgarde's defenders. The last the prince kept on his own person, and it was taken from him when he was slain in his chapel. Zengu rejoiced that the blood of Trollbane would haunt his people no longer, and brought together, the four sigils merged into one: the Sigil of Ignaeus.

In the Sanctum behind the chapel, the glowing lines of the Sigil of Ignaeus matched the etchings on Trollbane's tomb. In a flash of light the sigil was consumed, and the stone hands of the tomb released Trol'kalar. Zengu sent the blade on to Nimboya at Grom'gol, to end the Darkspear's slow progress in the forests of Zul'Gurub.

title: The Princess Beneath the Stones
body: Those who touch the Shards of Myzrael in the northern hills hear a voice pleading for help and feel a sense of security pulse through the crystal. She is Myzrael, she says, a princess of the earth, trapped far below by her captors the giants, and these shards are her only way to speak with the surface world. Her first request is simple. The Drywhisker kobolds of the gorge to the east, allies of the giants, keep a shard cluster like hers and carry motes of her power, and if the motes are taken from them and applied to that cluster, she will grow stronger. Some find their way to her through a pulsing pendant, which sends them a vision of a brilliant crystal in the northern mountains.
sources: gameobject_queststarter: Shards of Myzrael 138492 starts 642; Iridescent Shards 2701, Stone of Inner Binding 2702, Keystone 2688 start 651, 652, 653 and 688
notes: Converted: the opening is the setup of 642 (and 635 from the Pendant of Myzrael). Parts: 1 the gorge and the Stones of Binding (QUEST_DONE 651), 2 the Keystone and her release (QUEST_ACCEPT 653 Alliance or 688 Horde, offered at the Keystone), 3 the Twilight's Hammer and the stolen scroll (QUEST_ACCEPT 687, from Gerrig Bonegrip or Zaruk, left unnamed since each side meets only its own), 4 her defeat (QUEST_DONE 656 at the Shards or KILL 2755). Theldurin's warning and the scroll's repair stay Badlands' (330 on 692 and 709) and are only alluded to. Faction 0: 642, 651, 652, 687, 692, 656 are open to both; 653 and 688 are the Alliance and Horde branches. The Cataclysm version (Skuerto, Thenan) is not used. Checked: part 4 now QUEST_DONE 656 only, since the shackles are bound at the turn-in, not at the kill (4524 keeps KILL 2755). Part 2 reworded away from 4524 part 1. Gerrig and Zaruk stay unnamed; ironforge 153701 does not expose Gerrig.

parts.body: The gorge shards woke, and Myzrael felt more herself, though still far from free. Four Stones of Binding pinned her beneath the earth. With keys taken from the Stones of West, East and Outer Binding, past the guardians that watch them, the strongest, the Stone of Inner Binding, was opened, and she felt her shackles loosen. One lock remained: the Keystone, whose key, the Rod of Order, is held by the stone watcher Fozruk.

The Rod of Order was taken from Fozruk and set in the Keystone, and a shudder ran through the ground. The last lock had given way. Rejoicing, Myzrael said she would hide and grow strong until she was ready to face the giants, and that her rescuer would then be needed to summon her to the surface; an ally of hers knew how.

That ally welcomed the rescuer as a fellow servant of a higher cause. Myzrael's friends are the Twilight's Hammer, cultists who revere her as their Lady and long to bring her back to them. The means to do it, the Scroll of Myzrael, was stolen by one of their own, Theldurin the Lost, who lost his mind, scorned their teachings and fled; rumor places him in the Badlands.

The road led to the Badlands and to Theldurin, and in the end the summons was turned against her. Called up at the Shards before her power had returned, Myzrael raged at her rescuer as a fool, and was beaten. Her own Eldritch Shackles were bound to the Shards, an unhuman wail and a roar rose from far below, and the crystals that once promised warmth now pulse with open menace.

title: The Blackwater Expedition
body: Shakes O'Breen's Blackwater Raiders came to Faldir's Cove expecting to stay only a few hours, just long enough to raise a lost elven treasure and sail home to Booty Bay. Instead the sea rumbled, the tide fell away and two of their three ships broke apart on the Drowned Reef. Now the crew needs help. First Mate Nilzlix wants the wrecks' logs and charts recovered before prying eyes find them, and Captain Steelgut, who lost his Maiden's Folly and woke on the shore after the naga slew his crew, wants the Daggerspine made to pay. The gnomes Phizzlethorpe and Draxlegauge have made goggles to find the treasure in the dark sea, but first they must be charged at an enchanted stone in a cursed cave up the hill.
sources: quests 662 to 670 (descriptions, completion and reward texts)
notes: Converted: the opening is the setup of 663, 662, 664 and 665. Parts: 1 the gems found (QUEST_DONE 666), 2 Seahorn's word (QUEST_DONE 669, turned in at Booty Bay), 3 the naga attack survived (QUEST_DONE 667, the last of the chain). Faction 0: all quests have AllowableRaces 0 and the Blackwater NPCs are neutral (factions 120, 121, 35). Checked: part 1 reworded away from 4507 part 1. QUEST_DONE 669 confirmed unused by stranglethorn.json (Seahorn 3323 uses TALK 2487 and does not tell the find).

parts.body: Charged at the stone, the goggles worked perfectly, and through them the treasure showed plainly: elven gems crusted over with stone after their long years on the sea floor. The gnomes, wary after weeks among pirates of being caught holding the loot, sent the gems straight on to O'Breen.

A sample gem went south to Fleet Master Seahorn in Booty Bay as proof of the find. Seahorn was delighted, and with heavy things brewing at home and abroad, he trusted a top secret letter to the messenger for the stranded captain.

Then the Daggerspine massed for an attack, coming out of the sea to kill the one man who could steer the crew home. From the cannon on the high ground beside O'Breen, the naga were driven back and the Blackwater Raiders survived. They will sail as soon as the tide rises.
